doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Learning, living and the Colorado years
title: Making a living and studying with Dave Holland
summary: Lamb's landlord near Woodstock was Dave Holland, who had Lamb help him recover from heart surgery, changing Lamb's approach to improvising.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Has — this is sort of an obvious question but paying your rent as a musician, making a living, has there been ups and downs for you?

Sure. But never to the point of, you know, red alert. Never to that point. It always worked out. You know like after Rod left and I started the new Dry Jack thing, you know there was some financial struggles but like for instance right after that band broke up I moved into an apartment down near Woodstock and my landlord was Dave Holland.

Right? One of the greatest, to me, the greatest bass player on the planet and one of the greatest composers. So he was my landlord and I would go over and play with him all the time. He’d call me up and say, “I just got these charts from Kenny Wheeler, do you want to be come over and read through these charts?” Or, you know, and the big one was he had heart surgery — he had a valve replaced, and this was back in, man, ’82, so it was a little bit newer of a — it wasn’t quite so — the technology was very different. So his recovery time was long and he called me up and he said, “Would you be willing to come over two or three times a week for the next couple of months and help me get back in shape?” And that changed my whole thinking on my approach to improvisation. I mean this guy was such a master that I learned so much about relaxation, you know, expression to follow your — all of these subliminal kind of things that just altered my course improvisation-wise, composition-wise, and so that was a huge time in my life. And you know it was a struggling time financially but it didn’t really matter, other stuff was happening that was more powerful. But by the end of like two and a half months into it as he was getting stronger and stronger I started, I was like holy — I mean the elevation of his playing and the power of it and the, you know the lift. I was now rather than overjoyed by playing with him, blown completely away at this master you know, hanging out in his practice room playing with me. So that was —
Can you imagine what you would have had to pay a teacher to get that kind of stuff, and you still wouldn’t have got it anyway probably. The situation was just sort of perfect for you.
